summary: High request latency and fallback-to-legacy-model for Braintree integration during peak—customer escalated
description: Issue summary: During a Braintree Labs payment reconciliation job window (scheduled spikes between 03:30–04:15 UTC), a subset of API calls to the Redwood hosted inference endpoint experienced median request latency increases from ~60ms to 1.8s and a ~12% rate of automatic fallback to a legacy quantized model variant. Impact: Customer-facing batch jobs delayed, some reconciliation runs timed out and retried leading to duplicate downstream transactions and a billing reconciliation discrepancy reported by the customer. Environment: prod cluster in us-east-1, traffic routed through api-gateway -> smart-routing -> dedicated serving pool for enterprise customers. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run the Braintree reconciliation workload (described in customer-provided runbook) with concurrent workers >= 80. 2) Observe latency spikes after warmup period (~5–7 minutes) and increased fallback logs. 3) Check /metrics and SmartRouting logs for model selection decisions.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a synthetic load that mirrors Braintree: 80 concurrent clients, sequence lengths 800-1200 tokens, burst every 30s for 20 minutes.
2) Use rw-instruct-1.large pinned in customer routing policy.
3) Monitor /v1/streams and SmartRouting decision logs for fallback events.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered: (A) sudden kernel selection regressions causing increased per-token compute cost; (B) KV cache churn due to long sequence lengths and small effective batch sizes; (C) autoscaler not reacting fast enough to recurring bursts.
Findings: 1) Kernel profiling (runtime trace) showed increased kernel selection penalties for rw-instruct-1.large when sequence lengths exceeded 1024—runtime fell back to a safer but slower execution path in ~6% of calls. 2) KV cache hit rate dropped ~25% during the burst window due to numerous unique prefixes from parallel workers; this increased per-request latency. 3) Autoscaler logs show scale-up commands issued but constrained by per-customer quota; pool hit 92% and could not grow quickly enough.
Evidence links: dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ops/braintree-0309, runtime traces: https://internal.redwood.ai/traces/trace-789, related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1724
Partial mitigations during incident: temporary pool burst allocation, emergency SmartRouting config change to prefer variants with identical kernel paths, raising per-customer temporary GPU quota.

resolution: Workaround applied: temporarily increased dedicated pool capacity + SmartRouting preference tweak to avoid kernel-path mismatches. Permanent fix: merged runtime PR #1724 to align kernel-selection heuristics for rw-instruct family and a follow-up change to SmartRouting to include sequence-length-awareness when picking variants. Also increased default KV cache warmup window for enterprise pools. Rollout plan: staged rollout to enterprise pools in us-east over 72 hours with canary at 5% before full rollout. Customer credits: 20% credit for reconciliation runs during incident window applied to Braintree account.
